record.paper_title: Some open problems on the classical function space L1
record.original_question: What is the largest constant λ such that every subspace X of L1[0,1] that is λ-isomorphic to some L1(ν)-space must be complemented in L1[0,1]?

evidence.quote: Problem 6. ([10]) What is the maximal value of λ such that if X is a subspace of L1 which is λ-isomorphic to some L1(ν) then X is complemented in L1?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $L_1 = L_1[0,1]$ denote the Banach space of (equivalence classes of) Lebesgue-integrable real-valued functions on $[0,1]$ with the norm $\|f\|_1 = \int_0^1 |f(t)|\,dt$. For a measure space $(\Omega,\Sigma,
u)$, let $L_1(
u)$ denote the corresponding Lebesgue space with its usual norm.

For $\lambda \geq 1$, say that a closed subspace $X \subseteq L_1$ is $\lambda$-isomorphic to $L_1(
u)$ if there exists a linear isomorphism $T : X 	o L_1(
u)$ (for some measure $
u$) such that $\|T\|\,\|T^{-1}\| \leq \lambda$. A closed subspace $X \subseteq L_1$ is called complemented in $L_1$ if there exists a bounded linear projection $P : L_1 	o L_1$ with range equal to $X$.

Determine the largest constant $\lambda \geq 1$ with the following property: for every measure $
u$ and every closed subspace $X \subseteq L_1[0,1]$ that is $\lambda$-isomorphic to $L_1(
u)$, the subspace $X$ is complemented in $L_1[0,1]$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears to remain open. It is listed as an open problem in surveys on the classical space $L_1$, and although there is recent quantitative work on $(1+\varepsilon)$-isomorphic and $(1+\varepsilon)$-complemented copies of $L_1$ (e.g., quantitative Hagler–Stegall type results), no determination of the exact threshold constant $\lambda$ for automatic complementation was found in the search.

status_evidence.title: (1+)-complemented, (1+)-isomorphic copies of L1 in dual Banach spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Quantitative version giving (1+ε)-complemented, (1+ε)-isomorphic copies of L1 in dual spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Recent results address quantitative versions but do not settle the threshold constant for complementation of near-L1 subspaces in L1.

status_evidence.title: Complemented subspaces of Banach lattices
status_evidence.snippet: Survey-style results on when subspaces of L1 isomorphic to L1 are complemented.
status_evidence.claim: Related results give partial information but not the maximal λ.
